turns.prompt_text: I have a fish config, when I run it, I get his error: `config.fish:7: parse error near `end'` config: ``` # Mac Mini fish config # Add all subdirectories of the functions folder to the function path if test -d ~/.config/fish/functions set -l subdirs (find ~/.config/fish/functions -type d) #set fish_function_path $subdirs $fish_function_path end # Set local vars set -l fish_path '~/.config/fish/config.fish' # Abbrevations abbr -a fishconf "nvim $fish_path" abbr -a fishup "source $fish_path" abbr -a fishcat "cat $fish_path" # Unset local vars set -el fish_path abbr l 'ls' abbr ll 'ls -l' abbr lla 'ls -la' abbr la 'ls -a' abbr lt 'tree' ```
turns.response_html:
The issue is likely being caused by Non-Breaking Spaces (NBSP).

When you copy-paste code from websites or certain editors, standard spaces are sometimes replaced with a special character (Unicode U+00A0) that looks like a space but isn't. Fish shell does not recognize these as valid whitespace, which breaks the logic of your if block and causes the parser to choke when it hits the end statement.

The Fix

To fix this, you should delete the spaces at the beginning of lines 5 and 6 and replace them using your spacebar.

Here is the cleaned-up version of that specific block:

# Add all subdirectories of the functions folder to the function path
if test -d ~/.config/fish/functions
    set -l subdirs (find ~/.config/fish/functions -type d)
    # set fish_function_path $subdirs $fish_function_path
end

Why did this happen?

  1. Tokenization Error: Because of the hidden character, Fish interprets the start of the line as an unknown command or a corrupted string rather than a properly indented set command.
  2. Mismatched Block: Since the parser couldn't properly read the commands inside the if statement, it essentially "lost its place," making the end on line 7 appear out of context.
  3. Command Substitution: Your use of (find ...) is perfectly valid syntax in Fish, so the parentheses themselves aren't the problem.

A Quick Pro-Tip for Fish Configs

If you are trying to add subdirectories to your function path, Fish actually has a built-in way to handle completions and functions without manual find loops. However, if you prefer the manual approach, just ensure your config.fish is saved with UTF-8 encoding and standard spaces.

Validation Check: If you use an editor like VS Code or Neovim, you can usually toggle "Render Whitespace" to see if those spaces show up as dots (normal) or small symbols/different colors (NBSPs).

Does the error persist after re-typing those spaces, or are we back in business?

turns.prompt_text: `config.fish:7: parse error near `end'` Same error after whitespace tabs are converted to spaces
turns.response_html:
The error message you are seeing—parse error near 'end'—is a massive clue. That specific wording is a Zsh error message, not a Fish error message.

It is highly likely that you are trying to run or source your Fish config while your terminal is actually running Zsh (which is the default shell on macOS). Because Zsh uses fi to close an if statement instead of end, it hits that line and gets confused.

1. Check your current shell

Run this command in your terminal:

echo $SHELL

If it returns /bin/zsh, you are in the wrong shell. You cannot source a Fish configuration file inside Zsh; they use entirely different languages.

The Fix: Simply type fish to enter the Fish shell before trying to use your config, or change your default shell to Fish permanently:

chsh -s /usr/local/bin/fish  # Or the path provided by 'which fish'

2. If you are definitely inside Fish...

If you've confirmed you are inside Fish and it’s still happening, the issue is almost certainly the Non-Breaking Spaces (NBSP) I mentioned earlier. Simply "converting tabs to spaces" often misses these because they aren't technically tabs or standard spaces.

Here is a "sanitized" version of your config. I have stripped all potential hidden characters and replaced them with standard ASCII spaces:

# Mac Mini fish config

# Add all subdirectories of the functions folder to the function path
if test -d ~/.config/fish/functions
    set -l subdirs (find ~/.config/fish/functions -type d)
    # set fish_function_path $subdirs $fish_function_path
end

# Set local vars
set -l fish_path "$HOME/.config/fish/config.fish"

# Abbreviations
abbr -a fishconf "nvim $fish_path"
abbr -a fishup "source $fish_path"
abbr -a fishcat "cat $fish_path"

# Unset local vars
set -e fish_path

abbr l 'ls'
abbr ll 'ls -l'
abbr lla 'ls -la'
abbr la 'ls -a'
abbr lt 'tree'

3. How to verify for "Invisible Killers"

If you want to see if those hidden characters are still there, run this command in your terminal:

cat -e ~/.config/fish/config.fish
  • Standard Spaces will look like normal spaces.
  • Tabs will show up as ^I.
  • Non-Breaking Spaces or other hidden characters will often show up as code like M-BM- or similar highlighted blocks.

One final note: I noticed you were using ~ inside a variable string. While Fish often handles this, it is safer to use $HOME inside quotes to ensure the path expands correctly every time.

Are you running this from a fresh terminal window, or are you trying to source it from your existing prompt?
